how_peak_is_measured: TorchDispatchMode registers every tensor storage; weakref.finalize decrements on free; peak of the running total. The CPU analogue of torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated().
how_activations_are_isolated: peak(forward with grad) - peak(forward under no_grad). The difference is what is retained for the backward pass.
caveat: This run is fp32 throughout; the simulator models mixed precision (fp16 params/grads, fp32 optimizer). So ABSOLUTE bytes are not comparable and only stage-to-stage RATIOS are.

activation_rule_of_thumb.why_fsdp_stages_differ: The FSDP numbers are NOT evidence that activations differ by stage. My measurement is peak(forward with grad) - peak(forward under no_grad), which captures everything retained for the backward pass -- and under reshard_after_forward=False the GATHERED PARAMETERS are deliberately retained too, while reshard=True frees them. So ZeRO-2 retains more than DP and ZeRO-3 retains less, which is the transient side of the same memory/communication trade. Activations proper are unsharded by ZeRO; stages 0 and 1 are the clean comparison for that.
activation_rule_of_thumb.note: No pass/fail on the rule of thumb, on purpose -- I want the number, not a verdict against a threshold I chose myself.
